Article Title: 'Every Northeast family in Delhi asking - are we safe?' Rahul on Manipuri musician's killing
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday condemned the death of Manipuri musician Chongtham Vikram Singh, who was allegedly assaulted by a group of men in Delhi.In a social media post on X, Rahul questioned Union home minister Amit Shah and Delhi Police over what they were doing to stop the growing lawlessness against people from the Northeast in Delhi."Chongtham Vikram Singh ji, a renowned musician from Manipur, went downstairs to ask some men to lower the noise outside his home. He was beaten to death for it. A father, killed outside his own home, in his own country's capital. After many such incidents, every Northeast family in Delhi is asking the same question today - are we safe here?" the Congress leader said."What are Shah's MHA and Delhi Police doing to stop this growing lawlessness, especially against people from the Northeast? There must be a swift investigation, and the culprits must be brought to justice. My condolences to Vikram ji's family," he added.The 54-year-old Manipuri music teacher allegedly died after being assaulted by a group of men in Kilokari Village, in Delhi’s Ashram area, following a dispute over noise and nuisance outside his residence.According to police, Vikram Singh had objected to alleged shouting and nuisance by delivery boys and dhaba staff opposite his house. When he came downstairs to object, he was allegedly attacked with fists and blows.Vikram was taken to Holy Family Hospital by his son Yaiphaba for treatment, where he later succumbed to his injuries.According to the Police, a PCR call regarding the alleged beating of C Vikram Singh was received at Delhi's Sunlight Colony police station on September 7. Police said the preliminary enquiry indicated that Singh had objected to alleged shouting and nuisance by delivery boys and dhaba staff in front of his residence in Kilokari Village. When he came downstairs and objected, he was allegedly assaulted with fists and blows.The official further informed that they have registered an FIR under murder provisions and said all the accused, including minors, have been apprehended.Further investigation is still under way.
Article Summary: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi condemned the death of Manipuri musician Chongtham Vikram Singh. The 54-year-old Manipuri music teacher allegedly died after being assaulted by a group of men in Kilokari Village, in Delhi’s Ashram area. Rahul questioned Union home minister Amit Shah and Delhi Police over what they were doing to stop the growing lawlessness.

NEW DELHI: Telangana Police on Tuesday registered an FIR against BRS leaders KT Rama Rao , T Harish Rao, Gangula Kamalakar and others for allegedly obstructing and assaulting police officials outside the Telangana assembly.According to the FIR, the leaders allegedly abused women constables, threatened staff and caught police officials by the collar. Article Title: 'Delhi cops had audacity to go to Bulandshahr, arrest me': 'Influencer' Swatantra to HC; plea rejected
Article Text:

Counsel for self-styled right-wing influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj told the Delhi high court on Monday that the Delhi Police had the "audacity" to travel to Uttar Pradesh's Bulandshahr and arrest him in connection with the Jantar Mantar protest case."The SC has already quashed all the FIRs and the Delhi Police had the audacity to go to Bulandshahr and arrest me," the counsel was quoted as saying by Bar and Bench.Police, however, contested the claim and told the court that the FIR in the present case had not been quashed by the Supreme Court. The bench then sought a clear response from the Delhi Police, asking it to inform the court whether the FIR was "alive or not" and giving it the option of filing an affidavit or making a statement immediately, Bar and Bench report said.The police counsel also pointed out that Bhardwaj had been produced before a court following his arrest and was subsequently remanded to police and judicial custody.The HC rejected Bhardwaj's habeas corpus plea challenging his arrest in Jantar Mantar assault case.Meanwhile, a Delhi court extended his judicial custody by 14 days till September 21 in connection with the alleged assault on Sanjay Azad during the June 23.Bhardwaj was produced before Special Judge Saurabh Pratap Singh Laler through video conferencing from Tihar Jail after his one-day police custody ended.He was detained in Bulandshahr on September 4 and brought to Delhi, following which a court had on September 5 granted the police one day’s custodial interrogation. He was subsequently sent to one-day judicial custody on Sunday.The arrest followed outrage over a video podcast in which Bhardwaj allegedly claimed that he had "cracked the skull" of Azad during the Jantar Mantar protest and said the alleged assault attracted Section 307. He later claimed he had acted in self-defence. Delhi Police had earlier said Azad's injuries were simple in nature and were caused by a steel bracelet.Police subsequently added provisions of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and criminal intimidation to the FIR. A separate FIR under the POCSO Act was also registered following a complaint by the teenage activist alleging online threats and harassment after she spoke about the alleged assault on her father.
Article Summary: Right-wing influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj was remanded to 14-day judicial custody. Delhi court extended his judicial custody by 14 days till September 21 in connection with the alleged assault on Sanjay Azad during the June 23 Jantar Mantar protest.

Article Title: Balance needed between scientific probe and right to privacy, says SC
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Monday said technological advancements have made criminal investigation far more complicated and a challenge for the investigating agencies, as they get the stick from the court and the victim for not conducting the probe scientifically, and on the other hand, are accused of violation of privacy if they do.“A balance needs to be struck,” said a bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, while dealing with an application by journalist Abhishek Upadhyay, who claimed to be whistleblower on pilferage of Ram temple donations, and has accused Ghaziabad police of making an FIR in an alleged road rage case the pretext for seeking his digital footprints from June 1 from social media platforms to find his sources.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court said technological advancements have made criminal investigation far more complicated and a challenge for the investigating agencies. “A balance needs to be struck,” said a bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana.

Article Title: Purification row: Punjab Congress protests Haldwani ritual; demands FIR against organisers
Article Text:

Punjab Congress staged a protest on Monday against the BJP and RSS over a “purification” ritual allegedly conducted at Uttarakhand’s Haldwani Ramlila Ground after a Congress rally attended by party president Mallikarjun Kharge. The protesters also demanded that the FIR registered against Rahul Gandhi over his remarks on the incident be withdrawn.Congress MP Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa condemned the ritual and demanded action against those who organised it. "The Congress party in Punjab, and across India, does not believe in caste-based discrimination. We demand that an FIR be registered against the person who performed the 'purification' in Haldwani. The false FIR against Rahul Gandhi should be discarded immediately," news agency ANI quoted Randhawa saying.Former Punjab chief minister and Punjab Congress campaign committee chairperson Charanjit Singh Channi said the protest was against what he described as the “discriminatory mindset” of the BJP and RSS. "We have staged a protest against the mindset of the RSS and the BJP, specifically regarding the incident where the stage was 'purified' after Mallikarjun Kharge had stepped onto it.They treated the stage as 'contaminated' simply because a Dalit had set foot on it. An FIR must be registered against those responsible for this act. This protest serves as an expression of our anger and a warning to the government," Channi said.The protest comes days after Haldwani City Kotwali Police registered an FIR against Rahul Gandhi on August 30 following a complaint over his remarks about the ritual. The complainant, Amit Kumar, a 26-year-old Valmiki community member and office-bearer of Shri Ram Sena Dharmarth Seva Nyas, alleged that Gandhi's comments hurt the sentiments of the Scheduled Caste community.According to the complaint, Gandhi had on August 29 described the “shuddhikaran yajna” at Haldwani's Ramlila Ground as an act of untouchability and anti-Dalit discrimination. The FIR invokes provisions of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, and relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). The organisers, however, have denied that the ritual had any caste-based motive.
Article Summary: Congress MP Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa condemned the ritual and demanded action against those who organised it. Article Title: Fake encounter case: Allahabad HC seeks UP, Rajasthan Police reports over conflicting arrest versions
Article Text:
Allahabad HC has sought police reports after conflicting accounts emerged over the accused’s arrest in Jaipur and subsequent encounter in Firozabad

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Allahabad high court has sought reports from senior officers of the Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan Police after conflicting accounts emerged over the arrest of a theft accused from Jaipur and his subsequent involvement in a police encounter in Firozabad, news agency PTI reported.A division bench of Justice Ajay Bhanot and Justice Divesh Kumar Samant passed the order while hearing a writ petition filed by Riya Gautam, wife of the accused, Awadhesh. The court directed the additional director general of police (ADGP), Agra Zone, to file his personal affidavit regarding the encounter and asked the commissioner of police (CP), Jaipur, to submit a report on the arrest.Gautam had alleged that on December 5, 2025, around 10pm, police personnel reached the company in Jaipur where her husband worked and took him away without informing the family. A subsequent Rajasthan Police inquiry stated that Awadhesh was wanted in a theft case registered in Firozabad and that he was later sent to judicial custody there, with Jaipur police personnel accompanying the UP Police team.The high court, however, noted that the Rajasthan Police account was at variance with the FIR. According to the prosecution's version, an informer had tipped off the police about Awadhesh's whereabouts in Firozabad, where he and a co-accused were allegedly found near a cold storage.The FIR states that the accused challenged the police and attacked them with firearms, following which Awadhesh sustained a gunshot injury in the ensuing encounter.The petitioner's counsel alleged before the court that Awadhesh had been injured in a fake encounter allegedly carried out by police authorities to burnish their credentials. In view of the contrasting accounts, the court directed the ADGP, Agra Zone and CP, Jaipur, to place their reports before it. The order, dated September 2, also directed that a copy be sent to the CP, Jaipur, through the registrar general of the Rajasthan high court. The matter has been listed for September 17.
Article Summary: Allahabad HC has sought police reports after conflicting accounts emerged over the accused’s arrest in Jaipur and subsequent encounter in Firozabad. A division bench of Justice Ajay Bhanot and Justice Divesh Kumar Samant passed the order while hearing a writ petition.

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Monday announced bypolls for five Assembly constituencies and one Lok Sabha seat, with polling scheduled for October 6 and counting of votes on October 9.The Assembly constituencies going to polls are Nandigram and Rejinagar in West Bengal, Dharapuram and Madurantakam in Tamil Nadu, and Thattanchavady in Puducherry. He retained the Bhabanipur seat, from where he defeated Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee.The Rejinagar seat fell vacant after its MLA Humayun Kabir resigned from the constituency. In Assam, the Nagaon Lok Sabha seat was vacated after Pradyut Bordoloi resigned before the Assembly election and subsequently joined the BJP, according to reports.The EC said EVMs and VVPATs will be used at all polling stations for the bypolls. It said adequate numbers of machines have been made available and necessary measures have been taken to ensure smooth conduct of polling.The ECI statement reads, "The Model Code of Conduct shall come into force with immediate effect in the district(s) in which the whole or any part of the Assembly constituency going for election is included, subject to provision of the instruction vide Commission’s letter No. dated 2nd January, 2024."

Article Title: 'Kept on ventilator': Congress flags delay in proroguing Parliament, links it to delimitation Bills
Article Text:
File photo: Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh

Ramesh links delay to delimitation Bills

What happened during the Monsoon Session

Earlier setback for delimitation Bill

NEW DELHI: Congress on Monday questioned the delay in proroguing Parliament’s Monsoon Session, with party general secretary Jairam Ramesh alleging that the government was keeping the session open while seeking the numbers needed to pass the Delimitation Bills.Parliament’s Monsoon Session began on July 20 and was adjourned sine die on August 13 after 19 sittings. Ramesh said 25 days had passed since the adjournment, but Parliament had still not been prorogued.“Today is exactly 25 days since Parliament was adjourned sine die. But it has still NOT been prorogued,” Ramesh said in a post on X.He said prorogation normally takes place three to four days after a session is adjourned sine die, while citing the 28-day gap during the 2015 Monsoon Session as an earlier example.Ramesh referred to the 2015 session, which he said had been largely disrupted over the Lalit Modi issue. He alleged that the then Modi government had kept that session alive in the hope of passing the GST Bills, which required a two-thirds majority in the Rajya Sabha.He said the government was subsequently forced to consult the opposition more meaningfully before the Bills were passed later.Ramesh alleged that this year’s Monsoon Session was being kept open because the Union home minister was seeking a two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha for the Delimitation Bills.“The 2026 Monsoon Session has been kept on ventilator because the home minister is still scrambling around for his super-tainted two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha to get the Delimitation Bills passed,” he said.“How much longer before he accepts the reality that his politics of threats and intimidation has reached its limit?” Ramesh added.The remarks came after the government faced a setback in the Lok Sabha in April over a Constitution Amendment Bill related to delimitation and implementation of women's reservation.During the Monsoon Session, 12 bills were passed by Parliament, while 11 bills were introduced in the Lok Sabha and two in the Rajya Sabha.Only the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, was debated in the House, while the remaining Bills were passed without discussion amid opposition protests over issues including the NEET paper leak, alleged theft of Ram Temple donations and the police action against student protesters on July 20.The opposition had repeatedly disrupted proceedings during the session.The government had faced a setback on April 17 when a Constitution Amendment Bill involving delimitation for implementation of women's reservation in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies was defeated in the Lower House.528 MPs voted on the Bill, with 298 supporting it and 230 opposing it. A two-thirds majority required 352 votes.The defeat had raised questions over the government's ability to secure the numbers required for constitutional amendments related to delimitation.
Article Summary: Parliament’s Monsoon Session began on July 20 and was adjourned sine die on August 13 after 19 sittings. Ramesh said 25 days had passed since the adjournment, but Parliament had still not been prorogued. He alleged that the government was keeping the session open while seeking the numbers needed to pass Delimitation Bills.

Article Title: 2 BRS MLCs arrested over derogatory remarks against Telangana Speaker
Article Text:
Telangana Assembly Speaker Gaddam Prasad Kumar





HYDERABAD: Two Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) MLCs were arrested by police for allegedly making derogatory remarks against Telangana Assembly Speaker Gaddam Prasad Kumar.On Monday, Pollepalli Venkatesham, OSD to the Telangana Assembly Speaker, lodged a complaint with Saifabad police alleging that BRS MLCs Tata Madhusudhan alias Madhu and N Naveen Kumar had used derogatory language against the Speaker, who belongs to the Scheduled Caste community.The incident took place in front of the Assembly when BRS legislators tried to enter the Assembly premises wearing black shirts in protest against the alleged failure of the state government to fulfil its promises.When police stopped the two MLCs along with other leaders, they allegedly made offensive remarks. The complainant alleged, “T Madhusudhan and N Naveen Kumar Reddy launched a malicious verbal tirade targeting the Speaker, having knowledge that the Speaker hails from a Scheduled Caste community. They used derogatory language against the Speaker on account of his social background and constitutional role in place of public view. They acted with malice to demean the Speaker, incite hatred and cause public disorder.”Based on the complaint, a case was registered against the two MLCs under Section 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke a breach of the peace), read with Section 3(5) (common intention) of the BNS and the SC/ST (POA) Act on Monday night.Both MLCs were arrested from their houses in Hyderabad on Tuesday. They will be produced before the court for remand.
Article Summary: Two Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) MLCs were arrested by police for allegedly making derogatory remarks against Telangana Assembly Speaker Gaddam Prasad Kumar. The incident took place in front of the Assembly when BRS legislators tried to enter the Assembly premises wearing black shirts.

Article Title: Shiv Sena suspends 7 functionaries over Palghar hospital attack
Article Text:
Shiv Sena suspended seven party functionaries following an attack at Palghar's Relief Hospital





PALGHAR: The Shiv Sena has suspended six more functionaries in connection with the attack at Relief Hospital in Palghar, taking the total number of party functionaries suspended in the case to seven. The party officially announced the suspensions on Tuesday.The action comes a day after Shiv Sena Palghar city chief Rahul Gharat, the main accused in the case, was arrested and suspended by the party.The incident took place last Saturday following a dispute over the treatment of an injured man, Govinda, at the hospital. Shiv Sena functionaries and workers allegedly entered the hospital, created a ruckus and assaulted a hospital employee, triggering strong reactions.After Gharat was arrested on Monday, the party suspended him. On Tuesday, six more functionaries were suspended. They include district chief Kundan Sankhe, deputy taluka chief Manish Sankhe, district Yuva Sena chief Sairaj Patil, MLA Rajendra Gavit's son and deputy taluka chief Rohit Gavit, deputy taluka chief Rahul Sankhe, and Yuva Sena assembly constituency chief Hrishikesh Ware.In a letter issued on Tuesday, Shiv Sena secretary Sanjay More said the seven functionaries had been suspended on the orders of party leader Eknath Shinde for irresponsible conduct and violating party discipline.
Article Summary: Shiv Sena Palghar city chief Rahul Gharat, the main accused in the case, was arrested and suspended by the party on Monday. The incident took place last Saturday following a dispute over the treatment of an injured man, Govinda, at the hospital.

Article Title: Bombay HC dismisses Rahul Gandhi’s plea against summons over ‘commander-in-thief’ remarks against PM Modi
Article Text:
The Bombay High Court has refused to quash summons issued to Rahul Gandhi.





MUMBAI: The Bombay high court on Tuesday refused to quash summons issued to Congress leader Rahul Gandhi in a defamation complaint over his “commander-in-thief” remarks against Prime Minister Narendra Modi in connection with the Rafale fighter jet deal.A single bench of Justice N R Borkar dismissed Gandhi’s petition challenging an August 28, 2019 order of a Girgaum magistrate issuing process against him.The high court, however, continued for six weeks its December 2021 interim order that had deferred proceedings before the magistrate, allowing Gandhi time to approach the Supreme Court against Tuesday’s ruling.Justice Borkar said the court found no “perversity and illegality” in the magistrate’s order and therefore saw no reason to interfere.“This court finds no infirmity in the order. Hence, the petition is dismissed,” the HC said.The complaint was filed by M H Shrishrimal, who claimed to be a BJP member and alleged that Gandhi had defamed PM Modi through remarks made during a public rally in Rajasthan in September 2018.Shrishrimal alleged that Gandhi had referred to Modi as “commander-in-thief” while speaking about the Rafale deal and had also posted a video containing the remark on his personal X account.According to the complainant, the statements amounted to allegations of theft and hurt the sentiments of BJP supporters and others associated with the prime minister.Gandhi's counsel, Sudeep Pasbola and Kushal Mor, had argued that the complaint was frivolous and that Shrishrimal was not an aggrieved person with the locus standi to initiate defamation proceedings.The high court, however, declined to interfere with the magistrate’s decision to issue summons. Proceedings before the magistrate will remain deferred for six weeks to enable Gandhi to move the Supreme Court.
Article Summary: The Bombay High Court has refused to quash summons issued to Rahul Gandhi. The summons was issued in a defamation complaint over his “commander-in-thief’ remarks against Prime Minister Narendra Modi in connection with the Rafale fighter jet deal. The high court, however, continued for six weeks its December 2021 interim order that had deferred proceedings before the magistrate.

Article Title: MCOCA action against two accused from ‘Gold Hunters Gang’ in Kolhapur
Article Text:
Kolhapur

:





Special inspector general of police, Ranjan Kumar Sharma, has approved action under the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) against two alleged members of the “Gold Hunters Gang,” arrested in a gold chain theft case in Kolhapur.The accused are alleged gang leader, Vaibhav Narayan Adole (26), a Hinjewadi resident and native of Yerla in Amravati district, and Karan Gorakh Jagadhane (19), a resident of Vidhate Vasti in Aundh and native of Pimpalwadi in Paithan.Police said 28 serious cases, including forcible theft, housebreaking and vehicle theft, were registered against the duo across Maharashtra, including six in Kolhapur.They allegedly engaged an elderly woman in conversation before fleeing, on the pretext of asking for an address before snatching a 20gm mangalsutra from her neck, near Ambai Tank in Kolhapur.A parallel investigation by the local crime branch led to their arrest at Shirwal in Satara district. Police said 26 cases involving gold chains stolen from elderly women were registered across Maharashtra.The investigation found that the duo had allegedly committed offences in Kolhapur, Sangli, Satara, Sawantwadi, Kankavli, Kudal, Pune, Wardha, Buldhana, Beed, Akola, Amravati and Yavatmal.Superintendent of police, Nilotpal directed Juna Rajwada police station inspector, Kiran Londhe to prepare the MCOCA proposal. Havaldar Ranjit Desai and colleagues prepared it.Additional superintendent of police Annasaheb Jadhav, deputy superintendent Priya Patil, local crime branch inspector Sushant Chavan and assistant faujdar Sachin Patil scrutinised the proposal before sending it for approval.
Article Summary: Alleged gang leader Vaibhav Narayan Adole (26) and Karan Gorakh Jagadhane (19) arrested in Kolhapur. Police said 28 serious cases, including forcible theft, housebreaking and vehicle theft, were registered against the duo across Maharashtra.

Article Title: 'Grabbed hand and attempted to disrobe': Cab driver tries to assault woman passenger near Navi Mumbai airport
Article Text:
Police have registered a case and are searching for the accused driver (Representative image)





NAVI MUMBAI: A woman passenger travelling home after attending a party in Chembur allegedly faced molestation and an attempted assault by a cab driver who took the vehicle to a deserted road near Navi Mumbai airport late on Saturday night, police said on Sunday.The incident took place around 1.30am on the airport service road, about two kilometres from Navi Mumbai airport, police said. The accused allegedly stopped the cab on the pretext of drinking water before moving to the rear seat beside the woman, police said.According to the police, the woman was travelling to Panvel after a friend booked a cab for her following the party."The driver stopped the vehicle on the deserted service road, stepped out briefly, and then re-entered the car, sitting on the rear seat next to the woman. He allegedly grabbed her hand and attempted to disrobe her," said an official of the Navi Mumbai Police.The woman managed to break free and escape from the vehicle, following which the driver allegedly fled the spot.After the incident, the woman contacted her family and went to Panvel Police Station to lodge a complaint.Since the alleged incident took place within the jurisdiction of Navi Mumbai airport police station, Panvel police escorted her to the appropriate police station.Based on her complaint, Navi Mumbai Airport Police registered a case against the accused, identified as Mohammad Afzal Shaikh, under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Police have launched a search for Shaikh and are using technical intelligence to trace his whereabouts.Further investigation is underway.(With ANI inputs)(The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy as per Supreme court directives on cases related to sexual assault)
Article Summary: A woman passenger travelling home after attending a party in Chembur allegedly faced molestation and an attempted assault by a cab driver. The incident took place around 1.30am on the airport service road, about two kilometres from Navi Mumbai airport. The woman managed to break free and escape from the vehicle, following which the driver allegedly fled the spot.

Article Title: FIR lodged after 3,400 SIR forms found in Navi Mumbai shop; 5 BLOs suspended
Article Text:
An FIR was registered against Suraj Patil for illegally possessing voter enumeration forms





NAVI MUMBAI: The police have registered an FIR against Suraj Patil, a nodal BJP youth wing committee member, for illegally possessing and converting special intensive revision (SIR) voter enumeration forms for “personal use” and for breaking the maintenance of secrecy of voting under Section 314 of the BNS and Section 128 of the Representation of People Act.Section 314 of the BNS deals with dishonestly converting a movable property for own use, for which the punishment is at least two years imprisonment.The matter came to light on Thursday, after an advocate working for the Shiv Sena (UBT) noticed hundreds of original SIR forms lying at a photocopier’s shop in Kharghar. He alerted the police.The accused (Patil) had decamped from the Kharghar police station, leading to high drama throughout the night.Authorities seized 3,404 SIR forms, including 11 blank ones, of 11 polling stations from the photocopier’s shop next to the Ramsheth Thakur Public School in Sector 19, Kharghar, by Shiv Sena (UBT) nodal chief Balesh Bhojane.Five booth-level officers (BLOs) served with show-cause notices were suspended by the Panvel City Municipal Corporation (PCMC) chief Mangesh Chitale.They include three data entry operators working as booth-level officers from a private company, Saunik Integrated & Security Pvt Ltd, Bhayandar, engaged by the PCMC.Their names are Sulochana Mane, Prashant Mhatre and Rahul Bhagat.The Shiv Sena (UBT) had earlier warned the Panvel sub-divisional officer through a letter about various lapses in the electoral process.A two-member inquiry committee comprising a Panvel deputy municipal commissioner, Nanasaheb Kamathe, and an assistant electoral registration officer, has been formed to conduct a comprehensive probe.Bhojane said, “MLAs Jitendra Awhad and Rohit Pawar have tweeted the video regarding the original SIR forms at the Kharghar shop. We demand action against the Panvel SDO as he did not take preventive measures despite our complaint about forms filed at the BJP offices. The FIR was filed only after more than hundreds of our workers assembled at the police station.”After learning about the incident, Raigad district communication head of Shiv Sena (UBT) Prasad Bhoir lodged a complaint with the electoral registration officer.“Yesterday evening, the election registration office (ERO) received information that a person is xeroxing enumeration forms at a Xerox centre at Kharghar sector 19. Immediately, the assistant election registration officer visited the site and found that one Suraj Patil was holding around 3,400 enumeration forms and xeroxing it illegally,” Raigad district collector Kishan Javale said.
Article Summary: Police have registered an FIR against Suraj Patil, a nodal BJP youth wing committee member, for illegally possessing and converting voter enumeration forms. The matter came to light on Thursday, after an advocate working for the Shiv Sena (UBT) noticed hundreds of original SIR forms lying at a photocopier’s shop in Kharghar.

Article Title: Shiv Sena leader Rahul Gharat arrested in Palghar hospital doctor assault case
Article Text:
A Shiv Sena leader was arrested after a hospital ruckus involving injured Govindas

MLA seeks action against doctors





PALGHAR: Shiv Sena (Shinde faction) Palghar city chief Rahul Gharat, the main accused in the alleged ruckus and assault at a private hospital in Palghar, was arrested on Monday after he surrendered before the police.The incident took place at Relief Hospital in Palghar on Saturday night when five injured Govindas, who had sustained injuries during Dahi Handi celebrations, were admitted for treatment. Three of them were kept in the intensive care unit (ICU).The injured Govindas had alleged that the hospital was forcing them to undergo CT scans and was trying to charge them excessive amounts. Following the allegations, Shiv Sena office-bearers and workers entered the hospital late at night and allegedly created a ruckus. A hospital employee was assaulted and the IV lines of the Govindas admitted to the ICU were allegedly removed before they were taken away.Palghar police had registered a case against 17 people, including Shiv Sena district chief Kundan Sankhe, city chief Rahul Gharat, the son of MLA Rajendra Gavit and deputy taluka chief Rohit Gavit, under various sections of the law.“Gharat appeared before the Palghar police station on Monday and was arrested.Efforts are on to trace the remaining accused,” said Kishor Manbhav, senior police inspector of Palghar police station.Meanwhile, injured Govinda Akash Patil reiterated his allegations against the doctors. He claimed that although he felt better after being given an injection, he was allegedly kept in the ICU for three hours after being put on a saline drip against his wishes. He demanded action against the doctors.Palghar MLA Rajendra Gavit visited the Palghar police station on Monday and demanded that a case be registered against the doctors.Gavit alleged that the hospital staff were forcing the injured Govindas to stay back and undergo MRI and CT scans. He said Shiv Sena workers had gone to the hospital to help the injured Govindas and that a verbal altercation had taken place.He alleged that the doctors had filed a complaint against the Shiv Sena workers out of vendetta and pressured the police to register a case. “Can a patient not even question a doctor about an excessive bill?” Gavit asked, demanding that the police register a case against the doctors.
Article Summary: Palghar city chief Rahul Gharat, the main accused in the alleged ruckus and assault at a private hospital in Palghar, was arrested on Monday. The incident took place at Relief Hospital on Saturday night when five injured Govindas, who had sustained injuries during Dahi Handi celebrations, were admitted for treatment. Three of them were kept in the intensive care unit.

Article Title: 'Minor injuries, kept in ICU': Govinda group file FIR against Palghar doctor, threaten sit-in outside police station
Article Text:
Sena’s district chief Kundan Sankhe claimed they went to Relief Hospital after receiving complaints that the govindas were not being allowed to leave





PALGHAR: A fresh twist has emerged in the alleged assault of a receptionist at Relief Hospital in Palghar, with the injured Govinda participants whose treatment triggered the dispute filing a written complaint against the doctor at Palghar police station.A case has already been registered against 17 people, including Shiv Sena district chief Kundan Sankhe, in connection with the alleged assault.In their complaint, the Govinda participants alleged that although they had suffered only minor injuries, they were deliberately kept in the ICU and were not discharged despite repeatedly requesting the doctor to release them.They further alleged that the doctor ignored their requests, following which they sought the intervention of Sankhe. The participants claimed that unnecessary treatment was continued despite there being no medical requirement for it.The complainants have demanded that a case be registered against the doctor over the alleged conduct.Palghar MLA Rajendra Gavit, along with senior Shiv Sena functionaries, party workers and members of the Govinda group, gathered outside Palghar police station in support of the complaint.Gavit warned that the group would stage a sit-in outside the police station until a case was registered against the doctor.The latest complaint comes amid the ongoing controversy over the alleged assault of the hospital receptionist and the case registered against Sankhe and others.
Article Summary: Govinda participants claim they were deliberately kept in the ICU and were not discharged despite repeatedly requesting the doctor to release them. A case has already been registered against 17 people, including Shiv Sena district chief Kundan Sankhe, in connection with the alleged assault.

Article Title: Chandrapur Police Foil Cattle Trafficking Bid; 2 Die, 63 Rescued
Article Text:
Arrested cattle smugglers and the truck seized after Chandrapur police’s action

Chandrapur





: Sixty-five cattle being transported in cramped and allegedly inhumane conditions were intercepted by Chandrapur local crime branch (LCB) personnel at Pipri Phata on the Dhanora-Gadchandur road within Ghugghus police limits on Sunday. Two animals died at the spot, while 63 were rescued and shifted to a shelter.Police said the cattle were packed tightly into a 14-wheeler truck without adequate provision of food or water. The condition of the animals prompted the police to seize the truck and rescue the surviving cattle, which were taken to Pyar Foundation at Padoli for veterinary care.The operation led to the seizure of property worth ₹27.82 lakh, including the truck valued at ₹15 lakh, cattle valued at ₹12.60 lakh and mobile phones and other material worth ₹22,000.Three persons were arrested, the truck driver Omprakash Kawale (38), from Nagpur, and labourers Kaleem Malik (33) and Shahrukh Malik (30), of Uttar Pradesh. Three other suspects—Irfan Sheikh, Tausif Bhai Nizam Ahmed and Arbaz Qureshi—are absconding. The truck is owned by Javed Pathan of Aurangabad, said police.A case has been registered at Ghughus police station under the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, the amended Maharashtra Animal Preservation Act and relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. Further investigation is underway.
Article Summary: Two animals died at the spot, while 63 were rescued and shifted to a shelter. Three persons were arrested, the truck driver Omprakash Kawale, from Nagpur, and labourers Kaleem Malik (33) and Shahrukh Malik (30), of Uttar Pradesh. Three other suspects are absconding.

Article Title: Vijay tables bill to hike MLA vehicle allowance to ₹75,000, provide PA allowance of ₹25,000
Article Text:
Allowance hike

Chennai:





Chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday tabled a bill to amend the Tamil Nadu Payment of Salaries Act, 1951, proposing to enhance the monthly vehicle allowance for MLAs from ₹25,000 to ₹75,000 and provide a monthly personal assistant (PA) allowance of ₹25,000.The amendment follows CM’s recent announcement to provide a vehicle to every member of TN assembly to enable them to travel across their constituencies to discharge their duty effectively.CM’s announcement in the house was an outcome of a request from VCK legislator L E Jothimani, who requested govt to provide a car for first-time MLAs and those coming from humble backgrounds. “To give effect to the announcement, the govt have decided to amend TN Payment of Salaries Act 1951 suitably,” said the CM in the statement of objects and reasons.
Article Summary: Chief minister C Joseph Vijay tabled a bill to amend the Tamil Nadu Payment of Salaries Act, 1951. The amendment follows CM’s recent announcement to provide a vehicle to every member of TN assembly to enable them to travel across their constituencies.

Article Title: IUML MLA says his remark was distorted, support to TVK was on ideological grounds
Article Text:
Says support to TVK on ideological grounds

Chennai:





A day after alleging that ‘crores of rupees and ministerial berths’ were offered to them seeking support, Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) MLA Syed Farooq Basha said his remarks were distorted.Farooq Basha said in the assembly that his remarks made at an IUML meeting at Tiruvannamalai on Sunday were projected as an allegation against TVK.“I said that the DMK and AIADMK had come together and wanted an AIADMK leader to be made Chief Minister,” he said. But IUML rejected such a proposal because the AIADMK was aligned with the BJP , he said. “IUML cannot be swayed by money. We extended our support to TVK on ideological grounds,’’ he said.State minorities welfare minister A M Shahjahan, also from IUML, alleged that the two IUML legislators were confined in a hotel and intimidated to prevent them from supporting TVK.He said IUML was contacted by `DMK leadership‘ on May 7 with a proposal naming a CM candidate. “Another proposal was made on May 8. But we rejected it,’’ he said without elaborating.“On May 8, who took two Indian Union Muslim League members to a hotel and confined them there? Who threatened them? Who placed people to keep watch over us?” he asked.State PWD minister Aadhav Arjuna said a probe would be conducted on these charges.
Article Summary: Farooq Basha said in the assembly that his remarks made at an IUML meeting on Sunday were projected as an allegation against TVK. “IUML cannot be swayed by money. We extended our support to TVK on ideological grounds,’’ he said.

Article Title: Salem corporation council meeting disrupted over mayor’s demand for removal of deputy mayor chair from dais
Article Text: COIMBATORE: Tension flared at the Salem corporation council meeting on Friday when mayor A Ramachandran, who belongs to DMK, refused to conduct the proceedings, insisting that the chair of deputy mayor Saradha Devi, who belongs to Congress, be moved from the dais.The council meeting of Salem corporation, scheduled to begin at 11am, started 20 minutes late after the mayor entered the hall. Instead of taking his designated seat, the mayor sat among the councillors and declared that he would not preside over the session. He stated that during the previous council meeting, he had ordered to remove the deputy mayor’s seat from near the mayor’s chair. However, he alleged that the Salem corporation commissioner overruled his directive and insisted on retaining deputy mayor’s chair next to that of the mayor. “I will not conduct this meeting where I am not given the authority,” Ramachandran said.DMK councillors protested demanding the removal of the deputy mayor’s chair from the dais. When corporation staffers attempted to remove the chair, Saradha Devi launched a sit-in protest in the council hall. She accused the mayor of showing gender bias and disrespect.She said, “The mayor does not give me the respect I deserve because I am a woman.My chair has been right next to the mayor’s for the last four years; why should it be removed now? I respect this council, and I will not allow my seat to be moved.”Following the uproar, a closed-door reconciliation meeting was convened between the corporation commissioner, mayor, deputy mayor, and DMK councillors. Emerging from the discussions, Saradha Devi alleged, “They spoke about shifting my seat from the dais and asked whether I wanted the ‘chair’ or a ‘share.’ I made it clear that I only want my chair.”The deadlock remained unresolved. Upon returning to the council hall, mayor Ramachandran announced that all resolutions were postponed due to the disruption. He left the hall after that. However, Saradha Devi continued her protest.Tension between Congress and DMK councillors started after the national party left the DMK alliance to join the TVK govt in the state in May.
Article Summary: DMK councillors protested demanding the removal of the deputy mayor’s chair from the dais. When corporation staffers attempted to remove the chair, Saradha Devi launched a sit-in protest in the council hall. She accused the mayor of showing gender bias and disrespect.

Article Title: Kerala HC tells JFCM court to reconsider Ansiba’s plaint against fellow actor
Article Text:
Ansiba Hassan

Kochi

:





The high court on Monday directed the judicial first-class magistrate court, Ernakulam, to reconsider the complaint filed by film actor Ansiba Hassan against fellow actor Lekshmipriya and two others.The court issued the order in a petition filed by Ansiba challenging the magistrate court’s order declining her plea to register a case on her complaint alleging that Lekshmipriya and the two others had circulated videos on social media containing sexually coloured remarks against her. The bench of Justice Jobin Sebastian set aside the impugned order of the magistrate court and directed it to independently examine the allegations in Ansiba’s complaint and determine whether they prima facie disclose the commission of any cognisable offences and whether a police investigation is warranted. The magistrate court shall also consider whether a police investigation is necessary to collect evidence that cannot be effectively secured by the complainant herself.Ansiba, who is also a former office-bearer of AMMA, an association of Malayalam film artists, alleged that Lekshmipriya and two others had circulated videos on social media containing sexually coloured remarks against her with the intention of tarnishing her image and subjecting her to public humiliation.Previously, she had approached the magistrate court alleging that the police had failed to take effective action on her complaint and seeking a directive to register a case.However, the magistrate court declined Ansiba’s request for registration of an FIR, holding that the complaint did not disclose any cognisable offence and, at most, constituted an offence of defamation. Accordingly, it decided to proceed with the complaint as a private complaint, directing her to appear before the court to record her sworn statement. This prompted her to approach the HC. According to Ansiba, the accused had deliberately published videos on social media containing sexually coloured remarks, thereby outraging her modesty and seriously affecting her dignity and reputation.
Article Summary: Ansiba Hassan alleged that Lekshmipriya and two others had circulated videos on social media containing sexually coloured remarks against her. The court issued the order in a petition filed by Ansiba challenging the magistrate court’s order declining her plea to register a case on her complaint.
